title: COMPLETENESS-CRITIC supplement — national-regulatory specificity not covered by genericization-matrix.json
method: Reading-based transversal pass over ng.aiday.policy source documents (ul-it-policy/*/*.tex, with the densest national-regulatory detail concentrated in the per-document annotations-data.tex glossary-annotation entries), compared against every national-regulatory-relevant canonical anchor (kinds legal/regulator/jurisdiction/date) and a full string-grep of genericization-matrix.json. Rows below are concrete national-regulatory specificities (national statutes, national legislative venue/procedure, named national executive officeholders, national executive department, and an EU directive whose national reporting obligations are operative) whose suite-specific detail the canonical matrix does NOT already capture as its own anchor.

regulatorAnchors: ANCHOR-NATIONAL-SPOC-HCPN (HCPN as NIS2 single point of contact)
legalAnchors: ANCHOR-NIS2-TRANSPOSITION (PL 8364, incl. its article pegs and that it is the Luxembourg NIS2 transposition)
ANCHOR-NIS-REGIME / ANCHOR-AI-REGIME / ANCHOR-DATA-PROTECTION-REGIME / ANCHOR-EIDAS-REGIME / ANCHOR-TRANSFER-REGIME (EU-level instruments)
jurisdictionAndDateAnchors: ANCHOR-CRPD-RATIFICATION (CRPD ratified by EU and Luxembourg)
ANCHOR-NATIONAL-DATES (bundles 3 April 2026 ILR letter, 2 May 2025 SERIMA, 13 July 2018 / 26 January 2018 approvals)
coveredByMatrixForReference.note: The matrix covers the national regulators, the national transposition LAWS by their bill numbers, and a bundle of jurisdiction-bound dates. The rows below are the national-regulatory specificities that fall BETWEEN those anchors: the constitutive statutes of the named regulators, the national legislative chamber and parliamentary procedure, the named national executive officeholders, the executive department, and one additional EU directive (EECC) operative through the national reporting platform — none of which the matrix flags as its own anchor.

entries.title: National founding statute of the cyber-resilience commissariat (loi modifiee du 23 juillet 2016 establishing HCPN/ANSSI-LU)
surfaceForms: Luxembourg's High Commissariat for National Protection, established under the loi modifiee du 23 juillet 2016, placed under the authority of the Prime Minister within the Ministere d'Etat
ANSSI Luxembourg ... established as a component of the Haut-Commissariat a la Protection nationale (HCPN) under the loi modifiee du 23 juillet 2016
loi modifiee du 23 juillet 2016 (amended law of 23 July 2016) as the constitutive instrument of HCPN, GOVCERT.LU's host and ANSSI Luxembourg's parent
entries.genericDecision: The 23 July 2016 amended law is the jurisdiction-bound constitutive statute that creates the national protection commissariat and, within it, the national information-security agency. The matrix treats HCPN and ANSSI-LU as authorities (ANCHOR-NATIONAL-SPOC-HCPN, ANCHOR-NATIONAL-INFOSEC-AGENCY) but never names the founding law. Parameterize the citation to the national founding statute of the cyber-resilience/protection commissariat; keep the role (the agency exists by national law and sits under the executive), drop the specific 23 July 2016 date and the loi-modifiee form.

entries.rationale: Jurisdiction-bound national founding statute. The matrix anchors the regulators (HCPN, ANSSI-LU) but not the law that constitutes them; the loi modifiee du 23 juillet 2016 is a discrete national-regulatory specificity tying the whole cyber-governance chain to Luxembourg statute and the national executive. Per the saferDefault guardrail (generalize/parameterize preferred over keep for any UL/jurisdiction anchor), parameterize to a role-based national-statute reference.

entries.genericDecision: The transposition bills are attributed to, and deposited/voted at, the named single-chamber national parliament (Chambre des Deputes du Grand-Duche de Luxembourg). The matrix anchors the bills (PL 8364, PL 8307) but not the legislative venue or its unicameral first-constitutional-vote procedure. Parameterize the chamber name and the 'first constitutional vote' procedure to a role-based national-legislature reference; keep the fact that the instrument is national law passed by the national parliament, drop the chamber proper noun, the Grand-Duche framing, and the vote-tally specifics.

entries.title: Named national executive officeholders attached to the transposition bills (Prime Minister Luc Frieden; bill rapporteur Laurent Zeimet)
surfaceForms: deposited at the Chambre des Deputes on 13 March 2024 by Prime Minister Luc Frieden
Deposited at the Chambre des Deputes on 1 September 2023, with rapporteur Laurent Zeimet
entries.genericDecision: The NIS2 transposition bill is attributed to a named sitting Prime Minister (Luc Frieden) and the CER bill to a named parliamentary rapporteur (Laurent Zeimet). These are jurisdiction-and-mandate-bound real persons; the matrix person anchor (ANCHOR-AUTHOR-NAME) covers only the report author and named judges, not the national executive/legislature. Generalize to role-based references (the responsible minister / the bill's rapporteur) and drop the personal names, which timestamp the text to a specific government mandate.

entries.title: National executive department hosting the cyber-resilience commissariat (Ministere d'Etat / authority of the Prime Minister)
surfaceForms: placed under the authority of the Prime Minister within the Ministere d'Etat
HCPN ... placed under the authority of the Prime Minister within the Ministere d'Etat
Ministere d'Etat (Ministry of State) as the executive department of the national protection commissariat
entries.genericDecision: HCPN (and through it GOVCERT.LU and ANSSI-LU) is located within a named national executive department, the Ministere d'Etat, under the Prime Minister's authority. This positions the national cyber-governance chain inside a specific executive structure. The matrix anchors the bodies but not the hosting department. Parameterize to a role-based reference (the national executive department responsible for the protection commissariat); keep the structural fact that the commissariat sits under the head-of-government's authority, drop the Ministere d'Etat proper noun and Francophone form.

entries.title: Electronic-communications regime feeding national reporting obligations (EECC, Directive (EU) 2018/1972)
surfaceForms: unified reporting obligations stemming from NIS, NIS2, EECC, GDPR and CER directives
covering NIS, NIS2, EECC, GDPR and CER reporting obligations
entries.genericDecision: EECC (the European Electronic Communications Code, Directive (EU) 2018/1972) is listed as one of the five regulatory sources whose national reporting obligations are consolidated through the national notification platform (SERIMA) operated by the ILR. The matrix covers the NIS/NIS2/GDPR/CER strands but does not anchor EECC, which is an additional sector-specific EU instrument with national transposition relevance. Generalize to the composite set of reporting-obligation regimes channelled through the national platform, or add EECC explicitly to the regulatory-stack enumeration; keep the multi-regime reporting point, do not single out EECC as load-bearing for the policy claim.

Generalize/fold into the composite reporting-regime set.
